# Shenora

> Shenora (神阙) is a hybrid app framework for .NET 10 + React, on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS (NuGet: `Shenora` plus one shell package; npm: `@shenora/react`). The interface is a React page and the app's logic is .NET; Shenora is the shell that hosts the page, typed IPC between them, windows, native services, and modules for what .NET can do and the web platform cannot: media the webview cannot decode, background work, safe file changes and self-update, extra browsers. It is a framework an app is built on, not a server and not a UI component library.

A desktop app references `Shenora.Windows` (WinForms + WebView2, Windows only) or `Shenora.Chromium` (the kit's own Chromium shell through CEF, on Windows, macOS and Linux; the app's build fetches CEF). A phone app references `Shenora.Android` or `Shenora.iOS`, both over MAUI's `HybridWebView`. Each shell brings `Shenora`, which carries everything else. The page imports `@shenora/react`; `@shenora/cli` is a build-time devDependency that takes an app onto a simulator, an iPhone or an Android device. `Shenora.Launcher` is a native launcher that applies a staged update before a framework-dependent app starts.

Rules for writing an app on Shenora:

<!-- agent-rules:begin — a copy of README.md's block; doc-drift holds the two equal (D98) -->
- Reference ONE shell package and it brings `Shenora`: `Shenora.Windows` (WinForms + WebView2, Windows only), `Shenora.Chromium` (`UseChromium`, on Windows, macOS and Linux), `Shenora.Android` or `Shenora.iOS`. The page imports `@shenora/react`.
- Media, files, missions, updates and archives are namespaces inside `Shenora` (`Shenora.Modules.Media`, `Shenora.Engine.Files`, `.Missions`, `.Update`, `.Compression`), never packages of their own.
- Retired package ids, never to reference: `Shenora.Core`, `Shenora.Ipc`, `Shenora.Media`, `Shenora.IO`, `Shenora.IO.Compression`, `Shenora.WinForms`, `Shenora.WebView2`, `Shenora.WebView2.Sessions`. The IPC types are in namespace `Shenora.Core.Ipc`.
- Compose with `ShenoraApplication.CreateBuilder(…)`, one shell call (`UseWindows`, `UseChromium`, `UseAndroid` or `UseIOS`), then `Build()`. A desktop app calls `Run()` from an `[STAThread]` `Main`; a phone app calls `Start()`/`Stop()` from its lifecycle.
- `Build()` registers the framework itself (the dispatcher, the event bus, the kit's modules, the mission scheduler); an engine `Use…` call such as `UseMissions` changes what it registers rather than enabling it.
- A host route is a class derived from `ModuleBase` that names its `ModuleName` and switches on `request.Type`, registered with `services.AddIpcModule<T>()`.
- The page calls a route with `getBridge().invoke(module, type, { payload })`: the payload goes in the options object, and the module and type strings must match the host's exactly.
- For an error the page should show, throw `ShenoraException`: its code, parameters and message cross verbatim, so never build one from `ex.Message`. Any other arrives as `UNKNOWN_ERROR` with only its type name, a cancellation as `OPERATION_CANCELLED`.
- Keep `invoke` for quick calls: a route's synchronous part runs on the shell's UI thread. Start slow work with `post`, report with `context.Report(…)` and `context.Publish(…)`, and read it with `useShenoraEvent` or `useShenoraRequests()`.
- Call `getBridge().notifyReady()` once at page start: the host holds its events until then. It resolves to the `ShellInfo` the app declared (the `Shell` option of its shell or IPC bridge), or `undefined` when it declared none.
- Show a feature when `ShellInfo.capabilities` names it, never by sniffing the OS or the user agent.
- App logic for every shell goes in a plain `net10.0` project that references only `Shenora` and injects the contracts (`IUiDispatcher`, `IFileDialogs`, `IClipboardService`, `IUrlLauncher`); a WinForms, WebView2 or MAUI type there breaks the other shells.
<!-- agent-rules:end -->

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/README.md): what Shenora is, a quickstart, the package table and the status
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/getting-started.md): a new app from nothing to a window with a typed IPC round trip, on WinForms + WebView2 or on the Chromium shell, then onto a phone
- [The packages, one by one](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/packages.md): how the package set is shaped, and the basics of each package: the host, the IPC stack, the Windows shell, the Chromium shell, the React client, building the page's bundle
- [Mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/guides/mobile.md): the MAUI shells for Android and iOS, what transfers from the desktop and what does not
- [Media](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/guides/media.md): serving, probing, remuxing and converting media, the shell drawing the picture under the page, background playback
- [Missions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/guides/missions.md): the mission scheduler, with claims, lanes and a durable queue
- [File updates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/guides/file-updates.md): the journalled file-update queue, path locks and the staged self-updater
- [Sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/guides/sessions.md): extra browsers, off-screen, interactive and streamed
- [Adoption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/ADOPTION.md): bringing an existing WinForms + WebView2 app onto the kit in stages

## Reference

- [The wire reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/docs/reference/wire.md): the module names, routes, event types, error codes and capability names a page types, generated from the source
- [@shenora/react](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/src/Shenora.React/README.md): the React client, its bridge, stores and hooks
- [@shenora/cli](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/src/Shenora.Cli/README.md): the device loop, `shenora ios deploy` and `shenora android deploy`

## Examples

- [The Chromium sample](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/samples/Shenora.Sample.Chromium/Program.cs): a whole `UseChromium` app for Windows, macOS and Linux
- [The WinForms sample](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/samples/Shenora.Sample.Desktop/Program.cs): the Windows shell with WebView2
- [The MAUI sample](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/samples/Shenora.Sample.Maui/MauiProgram.cs): the same logic on Android and iOS
- [The portable module](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/samples/Shenora.Sample.Logic/PortableSampleModule.cs): app logic in a plain `net10.0` project that all three run
- [The sample page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiarongGu/Shenora/main/samples/Shenora.Sample.Web/src/App.tsx): the React side, through `@shenora/react`
